claims.text: Source-2 uses \(h_0=1\), proves specified negative-index terms vanish, and invokes expansion along a duplicated column, but only in an \((i,k,\mu)\)-lemma. [source-2@L1731-L1742|claim=formal-document]

groundings.excerpt:
1731: \begin{array}{lccrll}
1732: \ \ \ \ (h_{\mu_1+k-i-1},\ldots,h_{\mu_k-i},
1733:    &h_{i-k + (k-i)},&h_{\mu_{k+1}-i-1},&\ldots, &h_{\mu_{\ell}+k-i-\ell}&)^T \\
1734: = (h_{\mu_1+k-i-1},\ldots,h_{\mu_k-i},
1735:    &1,            &0,              &\ldots,&0&)^T.
1736: \end{array}
1737: $$
1738: Here we have used the facts that $h_0=1$ and that $h_{\mu_m+k-i-m}=0$ 
1739: for $m \geq k+1$ because $\mu_m \leq \mu_{k+1} \leq i$ implies 
1740: $\mu_m+k-i-m=(\mu_m-i)+(k-m)<0$.
1741: One then checks that cofactor expanding the (zero) determinant of this 
1742: $(\ell+1) \times (\ell+1)$ matrix along this duplicated column gives the asserted identity.
